name: PlanBench-XL
intro: PlanBench-XL 是面向大规模工具生态的交互式长程规划 benchmark，包含 327 个零售任务和 1,665 个工具。它评估 Agent 在工具可见性受限时能否检索可用工具、分解隐式子目标、处理缺失/失败/干扰工具，并沿长路径逐步恢复到最终目标。
build_method: LLM生成与过滤, 类型化工具合成, 状态图路径枚举, 可执行后端
metric: Accuracy, EGT datatype precision, Avg Turns, Mean EDT, Search/Call Ratio, ITCR, UIRR
task_type: Agent任务, 工具调用, 长程规划
eval_feature: 56种数据类型, 工具检索上限30, 最短路径5至9, 100轮上限, 三类保路径阻断
scale: 327个零售任务, 1,665个工具, 56种数据类型
task_type_en: Agent task, Tool use, Long-horizon planning
build_method_en: LLM generation and filtering, typed-tool synthesis, state-graph path enumeration, executable backend
eval_feature_en: 56 datatypes, retrieval capped at 30 tools, shortest paths of 5-9 calls, 100-turn cap, three path-preserving blocker types
intro_en: PlanBench-XL is an interactive long-horizon planning benchmark for large-scale tool ecosystems, with 327 retail tasks over 1,665 tools. It evaluates whether agents can retrieve usable tools under limited visibility, infer implicit sub-goals, handle missing, failing, or distracting tools, and recover over long alternative tool-use paths.
metric_en: Accuracy, EGT datatype precision, Avg Turns, Mean EDT, Search/Call Ratio, ITCR, UIRR

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18; status=source-reconstructed-awaiting-independent-signoff; scope=source-stage paper-aligned bilingual Build Process, fixed-source provenance, public-release boundary, implementation boundary, license boundary, and the source-stage topology contract. Primary evidence is the only arXiv submission, PlanBench-XL v1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22388v1; PDF SHA-256 593b053aacd52d4c436ca5a2a6b98d63de4760fa1c76b98f410b1371b8e6af61). Release evidence is fixed to official GitHub commit a0dacc2d227e197a61011a68d3b15c24aebbb2a1 and official Hugging Face revision 8d8d3d1a6fa7954a756193cf0f142c875a769b80. The code and HF query payloads agree byte-for-byte at SHA-256 aa708b84ae7d90a49bed5aadbe95fd0c420927f559fee2e4ace4e823132ad2a5 and contain 327 rows. The diagram corrects the former claim that all 1,665 tools are executable: the fixed release contains 56 datatypes, 185 executable baseline tools, 925 paired noisy tools, and 555 blocker alternatives, totaling 1,665 tools. Paper construction uses GPT-5.2 as both generation and filtering model. It first proposes retail datatypes, then removes vague, redundant, unreasonable, or unrealistic concepts. Candidate tools combine one to five input datatypes with exactly one output datatype; filtering requires deterministic dependency, externally grounded information access, retail-domain realism, and non-trivial information gain. The retained executable tools use five to ten aliases per datatype, code-generated alias-based names, GPT-5.2 descriptions, and fixed typed signatures. Each executable tool receives five explicitly described noisy counterparts: deprecated, condition-limited, stale, unreliable, and non-authoritative. The backend instantiates a complete structured retail record per case, uses non-trivial hidden values, resolves unique typed outputs, and fixes noisy responses across models and instances. A task is r=(D0,Y). State graphs add output datatypes only when required inputs are present; backward search finds inclusion-minimal tool sets, and legal execution orders form the process ground-truth path set. Empty path sets are discarded; multi-input tasks must genuinely need every declared input; retained tasks have shortest paths of at least five calls, with released lengths five through nine. Concrete values are sampled from the backend, GPT-5.2 verbalizes the task while hiding intermediate sub-goals, and GPT-5.2 executes one valid path to construct the gold target value. Runtime state is (q,Ut,Dt), with U0 empty and D0 available. Every model turn contains exactly one retrieve, tool-call, or answer action. Retrieval supports input-conditioned, output-conditioned, and joint input-output requests; aliases are mapped to canonical datatypes before exact typed-interface matching. A request matches no more than 14 executable tools, and the total response is capped at 30 after paired noise is filled evenly. Default retrieval exposes matched executables plus descriptive distractors. Optional block mode selects tools on valid paths, hides the selection from the model, replaces them at retrieval with explicit-failure, implicit-failure, or semantically misleading alternatives, and preserves at least one feasible path. Calls are legal only for previously retrieved tools whose required datatypes are present. Successful calls add trusted outputs to Dt; noisy outputs cannot become trusted downstream inputs. After each environment response, an explicit budget gate returns the trajectory to action selection while the visible 100-step budget remains and terminates only when the limit is exhausted; independently, a submitted answer ends the trajectory immediately. Paper correctness requires normalized gold-string containment and target datatype Y in state, preventing unsupported guesses. The seven paper metrics are Accuracy, Executed Ground-Truth Datatype Precision, Average Turns, Mean Explored Datatypes, Search-to-Call Ratio, Invalid Tool-Call Rate, and Untrusted Input Rejection Rate. Task completion groups Accuracy, Executed Ground-Truth Datatype Precision, and Average Turns; exploration behavior groups Mean Explored Datatypes and Search-to-Call Ratio; execution quality groups Invalid Tool-Call Rate and Untrusted Input Rejection Rate. Appendix G is represented as post-construction validation, not a filtering stage: five research annotators rate 50 tools and 25 datatypes, with means 4.32 and 4.56. Fixed data hashes additionally include datatypes 6eb6aebb91f31b464202fd9fd05811177f1d8fe0d0edaf2a22f7a1ef16846313, baseline tools b46dda31f10a2b427d82d3f58995b1201075c03f98cd3a14d7ec1a19217fd212, noisy tools 805d7a5b8b54ddd184d1358767914e69c8a4219fb0fa4bb41daaa92b40f0fcca, blocker tools 58e4148a18d58d1da30fdf35645a4b92843e4a1217ccd1513ed68d7aa1a1e7e8, tasks 924c018313fb9e2ea59152b30ab59d31f40c052a51732f515cbc49bb5b2e804b, paths 887bb9e0f17cd4c9105958694a6b8bba4cd4c88cb8835126dd609482ee5c33bc, and backend cd17e2f8b82c87af25c7a674bc2143e6b35bc84ec616760c1d25fb6e237215d8. Implementation boundary: the fixed evaluator also emits EGT recall, noisy-tool-use, and combined invalid-call metrics, but these are not inserted into the paper's seven-metric primary flow. Licensing boundary: the fixed GitHub tree has no LICENSE file, while the fixed HF dataset card declares MIT for the dataset; the repository code terms remain undeclared. The official project page exposes a leaderboard, therefore has_leaderboard is true. EN/ZH specifications have identical positioned topology, no edge labels, and dashed provenance edges. Strict Draw.io/XML and runtime visual review are required next; replacement formal assets and refreshed paper_aligned registration remain gated on independent reviewer approval.
